questions.title: Spurious parasite equated with coprozoic in this bank
questions.question: Spurious parasite?

explanations.A: Correct. This bank treats a spurious finding as equivalent to a coprozoic one. Both describe a foreign organism, or another species' ingested parasite stage, that passes through the alimentary tract and appears in a stool sample. Crucially, neither one ever truly infected the examined host.
explanations.B: Incorrect. "Temporary" describes the duration/pattern of an ectoparasite's host contact (feeding and leaving), not a non-infecting stool finding.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An incidental parasite is a genuine infection of an unusual host species, unlike a spurious finding, which is not a true infection at all.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since option A is the printed correct answer in this bank's own teaching, "none of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: State that this bank's teaching equates a spurious parasitic finding with a coprozoic one.

questions.title: Definitive host harbours sexual stages
questions.question: Definitive host harbours?

explanations.A: Correct. The definitive (final) host harbours the parasite's adult, sexually reproducing stage. This is the standard, defining feature of the definitive host role in a parasite's life cycle. No other host role in the cycle carries this sexual-stage function.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Asexual multiplication stages are more typically associated with an intermediate host, not the definitive host.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Larval stages develop in the intermediate host, not the definitive host.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An immature stage is, by definition, not the adult/sexual stage that characterises the definitive host.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: State that the definitive host harbours the parasite's sexual (adult) stage.

questions.title: Reservoir host: non-human source of infection
questions.question: Reservoir host is?

options.B: Harbours the parasite without being diseased
options.C: An additional source of human infection

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). A reservoir host is indeed a host other than man, but this is only one part of the full definition.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). A reservoir host often harbours the parasite without being diseased itself, but this alone is not the complete picture.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). Serving as an additional source of human infection is a key feature, but again only part of the definition.
explanations.D: Correct. A reservoir host combines all three features. It is an animal other than man, and it harbours the parasite, often without being diseased by it. It thereby serves as an additional source from which humans can become infected.

questions.subtopic: Host types in a parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: State the complete definition of a reservoir host, combining being a non-human host, harbouring the parasite without necessarily being diseased, and serving as an additional infection source.

questions.title: Modes of parasitic infection
questions.question: Mode of parasitic infection is?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). Ingestion of an infective stage is one valid mode of parasitic infection, but not the only one.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). Injection, as by a biting vector, is another valid mode, but again not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, but incomplete). Autoinfection, re-infection of the same host without external exposure, is a third valid mode.
explanations.D: Correct. Parasitic infection can be acquired through all three modes: ingestion, injection and autoinfection. The specific route that applies depends on the parasite species involved. Some parasites, in fact, are capable of more than one of these routes.

questions.learning_objective: List ingestion, injection and autoinfection as the modes of parasitic infection.

questions.title: Diphyllobothrium latum needs two intermediate hosts
questions.question: The following Platyhelminths require one intermediate host EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Fasciola hepatica requires only one intermediate host, a Lymnaea snail.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Schistosoma haematobium requires only one intermediate host, a Bulinus snail.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Fasciolopsis buski requires only one intermediate host, a snail.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Diphyllobothrium latum (the fish tapeworm) requires two intermediate hosts in sequence -- a copepod first, then a fresh-water fish -- unlike the single-intermediate-host pattern of the other three species listed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Diphyllobothrium latum as the exception requiring two intermediate hosts, against the one-host pattern of Fasciola hepatica, Schistosoma haematobium and Fasciolopsis buski.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Heterophyes heterophyes second intermediate host is a salt-water fish
questions.question: Salt water fish acts as second intermediate host in?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium latum's second intermediate host is a fresh-water fish, not a salt-water species.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Metagonimus yokogawai's second intermediate host is likewise a fresh-water fish.
explanations.C: Correct. Heterophyes heterophyes uses a brackish/coastal-water fish as its second intermediate host. Classically this is the mullet, Mugil cephalus. Cercariae released from the snail encyst as metacercariae in this fish before human ingestion completes the cycle.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since Heterophyes heterophyes correctly fits the description, "none of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Heterophyes heterophyes as the trematode using a salt/brackish-water fish as its second intermediate host.

questions.title: Schistosoma mansoni eggs are non-operculate
questions.question: The following Parasites pass operculate eggs EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Paragonimus westermani eggs are operculate.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Capillaria philippinensis eggs are operculate.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are operculate.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Schistosoma mansoni eggs are non-operculate, instead bearing a characteristic spine that helps them work through the venous wall for excretion, unlike the lid-bearing (operculate) eggs of the other three species listed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Schistosoma mansoni as the exception with non-operculate eggs, against the operculate norm of Paragonimus westermani, Capillaria philippinensis and Heterophyes heterophyes.

questions.title: Taenia solium needs only one intermediate host
questions.question: The following platyhelminths require two intermediate hosts EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Diphyllobothrium latum requires two intermediate hosts, a copepod and then a fresh-water fish.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Heterophyes heterophyes requires two intermediate hosts, a snail and then a fish.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Metagonimus yokogawai requires two intermediate hosts, a snail and then a fish.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Taenia solium requires only one intermediate host, the pig, which harbours its cysticercus larval stage -- against the two-intermediate-host pattern of the other three species listed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Taenia solium as the exception requiring only one intermediate host, against the two-host pattern of Diphyllobothrium latum, Heterophyes heterophyes and Metagonimus yokogawai.

questions.title: Eggs are the main pathology agent in schistosomiasis
questions.question: The main agent of Pathology in Schistosomiasis is?

explanations.A: Correct. Eggs are the main agent of pathology in schistosomiasis. Eggs trapped in tissue, whether intestinal, bladder, or hepatic, provoke a granulomatous inflammatory reaction around each one. This repeated reaction is what drives the disease's characteristic fibrosis and organ damage over time.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Living adult worms are comparatively well tolerated by the host immune system, having evolved mechanisms to evade it, so they cause relatively little direct damage while alive.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dead adult worms are not the main driver of chronic pathology either -- the ongoing, repeated egg-driven granulomatous response is what accounts for most disease.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since living and dead adult worms are not the main pathology drivers, "all of the above" incorrectly elevates them to the same importance as the eggs.

questions.learning_objective: State that eggs, not living or dead adult worms, are the main agent of pathology in schistosomiasis.

questions.title: Fasciolopsis buski infection via encysted metacercariae
questions.question: Infection with Fasciolopsis buski is through?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Skin penetration by a free-swimming cercaria is the infection route for Schistosoma species, not for Fasciolopsis buski.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Fasciolopsis buski eggs are not themselves the infective stage for humans -- the egg must first hatch and develop through the snail intermediate host into a cercaria, then a metacercaria.
explanations.C: Correct. Humans acquire Fasciolopsis buski infection by ingesting the encysted metacercarial stage. This stage is typically found on the surface of aquatic vegetation such as water chestnuts. Infection follows from eating this vegetation raw or insufficiently cooked or peeled.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Eating an animal's raw infected liver is a route associated with other, unrelated liver-fluke-type exposures, not with Fasciolopsis buski, which is an intestinal, not hepatic, fluke.

questions.learning_objective: State that Fasciolopsis buski infection is acquired by ingesting encysted metacercariae from contaminated aquatic vegetation.

questions.title: Schistosomulum is a cercaria without a tail
questions.question: Schistosomulum of schistosoma is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The schistosomulum is not merely a smaller version of the cercaria -- it is a distinct developmental stage produced after tail loss, not just a size difference.
explanations.B: Correct. When a Schistosoma cercaria penetrates human skin, it sheds its forked tail. The resulting stage is called the schistosomulum, the same organism now without its swimming tail. It has begun adapting to survive inside the host rather than in water.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The stage hatching from the egg is the miracidium, an earlier larval stage that infects the snail, not the schistosomulum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The cercaria develops and is released from the snail (the first intermediate host); the schistosomulum specifically names the post-skin-penetration, tail-less stage in the human host, not a stage inside the snail.

questions.learning_objective: Define the schistosomulum as a cercaria that has lost its tail after penetrating human skin.

questions.title: Trematodes require a snail as intermediate host
questions.question: Trematodes?

options.A: Require snail as the intermediate host
options.B: Have operculated eggs for all species
options.C: Always produce fork-tailed cercaria in their life-cycle
options.D: Possess parencyhmal cells in the body cavity

explanations.A: Correct. As a general rule, trematodes require a snail as their intermediate host. This generalisation holds across the group as a whole. The exact snail genus involved differs by species, but the snail-dependency itself does not.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Not every trematode species has operculated eggs -- Schistosoma is the well-known exception, with non-operculate, spined eggs instead.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Not every trematode produces a fork-tailed (furcocercous) cercaria -- that tail shape is specifically characteristic of Schistosoma's cercariae, not universal across the group.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trematodes are acoelomate flatworms with no true body cavity at all -- their internal spaces are filled with parenchymal tissue instead, so describing them as having "parenchymal cells in the body cavity" misstates their basic body plan.

questions.learning_objective: State that trematodes, as a group, require a snail as the intermediate host, while rejecting universal operculated eggs, universal fork-tailed cercariae, and a true body cavity as general trematode features.
